Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.
They said the sabotage could have been staged as a “false flag” operation meant to pin the blame on Kyiv.
The warning about the planned sabotage came from intelligence services in partner countries, though analysts at Polish intelligence agencies also raised the possibility of a provocation, the newspaper’s sources said. Rzeczpospolita reported that similar warnings were sent to intelligence services in the Baltic states: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.

Source: RBC-Ukraine
Russia opposes security guarantees for Ukraine modeled on  Article 5 of the NATO Charter, a source told RBC-Ukraine.
“The guarantees being discussed now, ‘something like Article 5 [of the NATO Charter],’ are essentially support for a European contingent from the Americans. Russia currently opposes this,” the outlet’s source said.
He said Ukraine currently prefers joining NATO, while guarantees modeled on Article Five, combined with maintaining a large Ukrainian army after the war, are viewed as a “Plan B.”
The Washington Post reported on November 22 that Vladimir Putin had privately agreed Kyiv could receive security guarantees similar to Article 5 of the NATO Charter once the war ends, but without Ukraine joining the alliance. U.S. negotiators are also considering offering Russia all of Donbas in exchange for Ukraine’s entry into NATO, the newspaper reported.

The wife of a Japanese journalist arrested in Russia has made her first public comments since his detention last month, ramping up pressure on authorities to secure his release.
In a handwritten letter shared with The Moscow Times, Nozomi Imai called for her husband, Yuki, to be freed from a Moscow prison, saying she and his parents have spent “every day worrying about him.”
“It has now been more than a month since my husband was detained. Since that day, our family has remained trapped in grief,” she wrote in the letter.
Yuki Imai, a 34-year-old reporter for The Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, was arrested on espionage charges last month in the Far East city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk. The incident marked the highest-profile detention of a foreign journalist in Russia since 2023’s arrest of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich.

The bomb, reportedly a German-made device from World War II, was transported under police escort to the central training area in Harju County on Tuesday.
The Western Estonia Bomb Disposal Unit (Lääne-Eesti pommigrupp) is now preparing to render the device safe.
A metal detectorist had discovered the 250-kilogram aerial bomb about 30 centimeters underground in a field in Lemmetsa village just north of Pärnu City on Sunday.
Thanks to its considerable destructive power, the bomb could not be destroyed at the Rescue Board's usual demolition site in nearby Potsepa.

By Christian Parkinson Reporting from Johannesburg

A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.
The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.
Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa.
He is one of five Zimbabweans who were arrested at OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg on 8 November. South African prosecutors have not confirmed which side the Zimbabweans allegedly intended to fight for.
Sothole's four co-accused have yet to enter pleas and are due to return to the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court on 1 December for further plea and sentencing proceedings.
Another four Zimbabweans were arrested at a hotel in Johannesburg at the same time in a joint operation and are facing a different court process.

Článek
Britské ministerstvo obrany a domácí tajná služba MI5 dnes varovaly firmy, které přímo podporují ukrajinskou armádu, že jim hrozí zvýšené riziko sabotáže ze strany Ruska. Informovala o tom agentura Reuters, podle níž jde o velmi neobvyklé veřejné oznámení. Hundreds of schools in Germany and Denmark receive bomb threats
November 23, 2026, 10:31 pm
Source: Bloomberg
Schools in Germany and Denmark have received bomb threats. Authorities in both countries are investigating and believe the threats were hoaxes.
In Denmark, the threats were emailed to several schools across the country. Police said they saw no need at this point to evacuate schools or take special security measures.
In Germany, about 450 schools nationwide received threats, including schools in Berlin, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, and Thuringia.
Since mid-October, schools in several European countries, as well as airlines, airports, and media outlets, have received false bomb threats. It remains unclear who sent the messages. The Financial Times reported that European intelligence agencies are looking into whether Russia was involved in sending the threats.

Explosions and shrapnel accounted for 92% of recorded Russian military deaths in the war against Ukraine. The investigative outlet iStories highlighted the figure after reviewing a database of Russian front-line military losses compiled by Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency, and shared by hackers. Meduza and other news outlets reviewed the same data at the same time.
Gunfire accounted for only 1.3% of deaths. Other, even less common causes included coronary heart disease (about 2,000 deaths), suicide (about 1,300), and pneumonia (about 700).
Based on their analysis of the database, Meduza and Mediazona calculated that at least 720,000 Russian service members had died in the war against Ukraine by fall 2026.

Volk said investigators were also looking into suspected transfers to foreign bank accounts using falsified documents.

Skip to main content
explainers
Putin is reportedly open to Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine. But what does Article 5 actually say? Would the guarantees require NATO members to go to war if Russia attacks again?
7 cards
November 23, 2026, 4:30 pm
Contents
1
What happened?
Sources close to the U.S. negotiating team led by Donald Trump’s special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner said a ceasefire or a peace deal to end Russia’s war against Ukraine could include security guarantees for Kyiv modeled on Article 5 of NATO’s founding treaty, or even full NATO membership for Ukraine.

Bombendrohungen an Hunderten Schulen bundesweit

Freiburg, Erfurt oder Hamburg: Hunderte Schulen im ganzen Land haben Drohschreiben bekommen. Mehrere Schulen wurden vorsorglich geräumt. Laut verschiedenen Polizeibehörden gibt es aber keine Hinweise auf eine konkrete Gefahr.
An zahlreichen Schulen bundesweit gibt es aktuell Bombendrohungen. Entsprechende E-Mails seien am Morgen unter anderem in Jena, Erfurt, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt und Greiz in Thüringen eingegangen, teilte etwa die Landespolizeidirektion in Erfurt mit. Auch andere Bundesländer seien betroffen, hieß es. Einzelne Schulen, etwa in Freiburg, wurden vorsorglich geräumt.
Die Polizei in Thüringen geht nach eigenen Angaben nicht davon aus, dass die Drohungen ernst gemeint sind. Den Schulen werde empfohlen, die Einrichtungen nicht zu räumen und den Schulbetrieb normal fortzusetzen. Zu den Verfassern der Schreiben lägen keine Erkenntnisse vor.

Details: The brigade did not specify when exactly the strikes took place but noted that the combat mission was carried out by a pilot named Andrii within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Army Corps.

Die E-Mails hatten laut den Einsatzkräften alle denselben Wortlaut.








Berlin – Etwa 450 Schulen in Deutschland haben am Montagmorgen Bombendrohungen per E-Mail erhalten. Die Schreiben mit dem Betreff "Der Tod erwartet dich" hätten nach Angaben der Polizei alle denselben Wortlaut, berichtete die "Bild"-Zeitung. Die Polizei in Freiburg bestätigte, dass unter anderem über den Notruf Meldungen über angebliche Bombendrohungen an vielen Schulen eingegangen seien. "Nach derzeitigen Erkenntnissen wurden die Drohungen landesweit per E-Mail an über 450 Schulen verschickt." Von wem die Drohschreiben stammten, müsse nun ermittelt werden.

An zahlreichen Schulen in Deutschland gibt es aktuell Bombendrohungen. Entsprechende E-Mails seien zum Beispiel am Morgen unter anderem in Jena, Erfurt, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt und Greiz in Thüringen eingegangen, teilte etwa die Landespolizeidirektion in Erfurt heute mit. Auch andere Bundesländer seien betroffen, hieß es.
Die Polizei in Thüringen geht nach eigenen Angaben nicht davon aus, dass die Drohungen ernst gemeint sind. Den Schulen werde empfohlen, die Einrichtungen nicht zu räumen und den Schulbetrieb normal fortzusetzen. Zu den Verfassern der Schreiben lägen keine Erkenntnisse vor.
Auch in Niedersachsen gibt es Bombendrohungen gegen mehrere Schulen. Das bestätigten das Innenministerium und das Kultusministerium in Hannover der dpa. Zum Inhalt der Drohungen und zum Ausmaß, wie viele Schulen davon betroffen sind, machten die Ministerien keine Angaben.
